summary: SSE stream accumulates unfinished choice fragments after CDN buffering and reconnect
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after intermittent connectivity through their CDN, SSE-based streams reconnect but the resumed stream contains accumulated partial token fragments that create malformed JSON choices or appear duplicated. Impact: customer experiences corrupted final choices or truncated completions requiring users to retry; affects production traffic for NovelChat (enterprise). Environment: production, us-west region, requests routed via Fastly CDN -> API gateway -> streaming service. Observed since 2026-03-11 22:40 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Client opens SSE connection to /v1/streams with session-id and receives partial choice tokens; 2) Introduce a synthetic upstream stall at CDN edge (simulate buffering + TCP connection close after keepalive); 3) Client reconnects using same session-id and last-offset header; 4) Server resumes and emits a mix of old partial fragments and new tokens; 5) Client assembles choices and JSON becomes malformed or contains duplicated token substrings.

investigation_notes: Checked resume logic: server accepts resume-offset and replays remaining buffer from session store.
Pending-prefix metric showed non-zero pending bytes for resumed sessions behind Fastly edge only.
Observed sequence where CDN closes connection after buffering part of an in-flight chunk; Fastly replays a cached tail during revalidation causing overlapped fragments.
Hypothesis: CDN/edge buffering + HTTP/2 multiplexing results in duplicate TCP segments reaching gateway which triggers duplicate partial writes that are reassembled by client on resume.
Reproduced locally by forcing a buffered close at the pseudo-edge and then reconnecting client with the same resume-offset; confirmed duplicated substring occurrence.
Checked streaming runtime: prefix reassembly does not dedupe overlapping byte ranges when applyPendingPrefix is true; needs defensive checks for identical token boundaries.
API gateway logs show keepalive timeout differences between edge and backend causing resume with offset that points inside a previously sent partial fragment (offset math off-bytes vs tokens).
Customer traces include X-Request-ID: 1a2b3c-resume that maps to internal trace r-77b; full trace captured and attached to PR referenced above.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support): Initial report received from NovelChat support contact. Attached their sample payloads and browser console capture.
Miguel Santos (SRE): Running live repro against staging with Fastly in front; able to reproduce 3/5 attempts. Captured pcap and chunk boundaries.
SRE follow-up: Creating INT-2119 to coordinate with network infra to inspect Fastly config and probe timeouts.
Customer: "We see this intermittently across web and mobile SDK — it mostly happens when a user on poor mobile network reconnects behind the CDN."
Eng (runtime): Adding guard in resume path to validate that incoming resume-offset aligns to token boundary or previously-acked event length. Will propose small change to replay logic.
Support: Notifying customer of workaround: client should prefer exponential backoff and request a fresh session on repeated resume failures.
resolution: In progress - temporary mitigation recommended: update client SDK to detect malformed final choices and fall back to a full new request after 1 failed resume attempt. Engineering proposed fix: validate resume-offset against session fragment map and drop overlapping pending-prefix bytes before stitching. Patch PR created: serving-runtime PR #1284. Follow-up actions: coordinate with CDN/edge team to lower buffering at Fastly for SSE endpoints and add metric for pending-prefix-length > 0 on resumed sessions. Customer notified of workarounds on 2026-03-12.
